instructions: Chop the cherry tomatoes small. Set a sieve over a bowl, add the tomatoes and press down on them to push out the juice and seeds. Discard the juice.
Finely chop the onion and slice the green onions. Shred the basil, mint and parsley. Add all of it to the drained tomatoes, along with the crumbled feta.
In a separate bowl, whisk 1 1/2 cups flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Stir it into the tomato mixture.
Pour in 2/3 cup chilled soda water and stir until it comes together as a thick batter. It will look too dry at first, but keep stirring.
Heat a large frying pan over medium heat. Add 2 tbsp of the oil and wait until it shimmers.

Scoop about 1/4 cup of batter into the pan for each fritter and flatten it with the back of the spoon. Fry 5 or 6 fritters at a time for 3 minutes on each side, until golden. Stand back a little, they can spatter.
Transfer them to a plate lined with paper towels. Add 2 tbsp of oil to the pan before each new batch. You should get about 18 fritters.
Taste one. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt to the rest of the batter before you fry it.
Serve hot or cold with the Greek yogurt. For packed lunches, keep the fritters in the fridge for up to 2 days and warm them in a 350°F oven for 8 minutes.
method_notes: Not Quite Nigella is the lead (5 from 64 ratings): tomatoes pressed in a sieve, onion, spring onion and basil, mint and parsley, folded into a flour and baking powder batter loosened with chilled soda water and shallow fried about 3 minutes a side. Coley Cooks and Great British Chefs agree on the tomato and herb base and add feta, which the lead doesn't have, so a small amount is added to match the list. Cold fritters are fine in the sources, which is why this counts as a make-ahead lunch even though the frying takes about 35 minutes in total.
